issues.detail: The Greek 'επαραντες δε τους οφθαλμους αυτων' (lifting up their eyes) is a participle describing the subjects. The Vietnamese translation 'Ngước mắt lên' (Looking up) is phrased as an imperative command (Look up!) rather than a description of what they did.
The Greek 'ουδενα ειδον' (I saw no one) is first-person singular. The Vietnamese 'họ không thấy' (they did not see) changes the subject from 'I' to 'they'.
